text: The initial blood work is inconclusive regarding infection or inflammation, so I need more details on the skin lesions themselves. Have the blisters on your forearm ruptured to leave painful erosions, and do they appear on other parts of your body besides your forearm?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.

The clinical presentation of mucosal ulcers, skin blisters, and recent initiation of captopril and discontinuation of meloxicam is highly suggestive of a severe drug reaction. Given the severity and the specific medication history, I need to confirm the extent of the skin detachment to differentiate between SJS and TEN. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination showing extent of erythema and blistering.
